ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two horizontal straight lines, marked on the left with identical pink arrows to indicate that they are parallel. A diagonal line slanting down to the right goes from the upper left through the upper intersection, then to the lower right through the lower right intersection, serving as a transversal. ∠6 is located below the upper horizontal line and to the right of this diagonal transversal slanting down to the right; ∠14 is located below the lower horizontal line and to the right of the same diagonal transversal slanting down to the right. Reasoning: The problem gives m∠14 = 38. Since the two horizontal lines are parallel, and the same transversal cuts them, ∠6 and ∠14 are corresponding angles, so they are equal. Therefore m∠6 = m∠14 = 38.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as two horizontal parallel lines cut by the right-slanting diagonal transversal. Identify angle 6 at the top intersection as the angle below the upper parallel line and to the right of the right-slanting transversal. Identify angle 14 at the lower-right intersection as the angle below the lower parallel line and to the right of the same transversal. From the text, use m∠14 = 38. Since corresponding angles formed by a transversal cutting parallel lines are congruent, m∠6 = m∠14 = 38.
